tldr: This thread is a running stream of reinforcement-learning preprints, not one event; it was reclustered from a broader LLM-knowledge reading list. From Oct 21 the papers moved from agentic RL over stateful environments and credit assignment to training-stack fixes, then to multi-agent and long-horizon web agents in early November.
whats_new: Nov 9: the MaxIM preprint trains incremental summarization with RL so an agent keeps a bounded memory of an unbounded interaction history, optimized for downstream task utility.
why_it_matters: RL is becoming the default post-training tool for agents, and these papers locate where it breaks: credit assignment across turns, inference/training numeric mismatch, rollout cost and memory limits.

beats.headline: Agentic RL moves to stateful environments and per-decision credit
beats.summary: Early papers train small models on data-centric tasks and give search agents awareness of what they already retrieved.

beats.headline: Training-stack plumbing: rounding mismatch, a SageMaker guide and a robust-RL benchmark
RL aimed at agent failures: hallucination abstention, terminal misbehavior and harness co-design
Confidence calibration, self-learning and hierarchical skill routing
Multi-agent RL, long-horizon web agents and prompt compression
A skeptical audit: multi-turn RL gains hinge on sampling breadth and interaction depth
Rollout cost takes over: few-step diffusion RL, async scheduling and world-model memory
RL-trained summarization for bounded agent memory

open_questions: Do multi-turn RL gains survive when interaction depth and sampling budget match a production agent's limits?
Does rounding-location alignment become a default in open RL stacks that separate inference and training engines?
Does RL-trained memory summarization like MaxIM beat plain truncation or retrieval on long-running agent tasks?
Will any of these methods ship with code that runs on managed services such as SageMaker MTRL?
take_for_builders: Before running RL post-training on an agent, check that your inference and training engines produce matching log-probs, and size rollout budgets against the Nov 4 depth/breadth findings; treat the rest as unreplicated preprints.
